args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest deploy) was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of 18%. Rolled back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Post-rollback status: healthy, error rate 0.2%. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging before v2.3.1 was promoted. Follow-up: root-cause v2.3.1 and review why the release was promoted despite the unhealthy staging candidate.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three regions and opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged the on-call engineer.

- **Before:** The latest deploy, v2.3.1, was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that had been healthy in production. After the rollback, all three regions run v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback and the results afterwards.

The test version of v2.3.1 was already failing in staging before v2.3.1 went to production. I added this to the incident as a follow-up, along with finding the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
